sheet-23.description: Sheet 23 of the Sanborn Gloucester City series, dated January 1923, covers the Highland Park subdivision at 100 feet to an inch, with north towards the upper left. The streets are drawn on a grid turned about 34 degrees to the sheet. Klemm Avenue runs along the south side of the railroad lettered C. G. & M. E. R.R. (P. & R. Ry.), which crosses the upper part of the sheet; Highland Boulevard, Park Avenue and Sherwood Avenue run parallel to it, and Greenwood, Roseland, Sylvan, Orlando and Palace Avenues cross them. Amon Avenue and Baynes Avenue meet in the lower left corner, where dash-dot city limit lines cross the blocks, and Market runs along the bottom edge. Beyond Sherwood Avenue a line of narrow lots faces a large open block (272) crossed by the P.R.R. freight line. The South Branch of Newton Creek winds across the top of the sheet above the railroad, and a second creek runs from the railroad down the right side, past large undivided blocks (260, 266, 267) and a street marked not named; a short row of dwellings (block 261) lies at the upper right. The subdivision is laid out in narrow numbered lots, mostly vacant, with scattered one and two storey frame dwellings and garages, concentrated near Highland Boulevard and Roseland and Sylvan Avenues. Named buildings are the Highland Park Fire Department and a Presbyterian church, both in the blocks between Klemm Avenue and Highland Boulevard. Water pipes and hydrants are marked along several streets. The upper left corner holds the compass rose and a field of vacant lots on a street marked not open; an outlined blank area lies at the left edge, and the number 18 there refers to the adjoining sheet.
notes: Printed as sheet 23 of the Gloucester City, N.J. series (Jan. 1923); the sheet title is Highland Park. The area lies in Gloucester City today (parcel municipality code 0414).
Roseland Avenue is Rosalind Avenue in OpenStreetMap.
Palace Avenue is not in OpenStreetMap.
The railroad along Klemm Avenue is lettered C. G. & M. E. R.R. (P. & R. Ry.); a P.R.R. freight line crosses block 272.
Baynes Avenue, Amon Avenue and Market were left out of the control: curved, at the sheet edge, and the modern Baynes / Market junction does not match the drawing.

Printed sheet 23 of the Gloucester City series (Jan. 1923), titled Highland Park; 100 ft to an inch; north to upper left, grid turned about 34 deg. One part: Klemm Av, Highland Blvd, Park Av, Sherwood Av crossed by Greenwood, Roseland (now Rosalind), Sylvan, Orlando, Palace Avs; Amon and Baynes Avs and Market at lower left; South Branch of Newton Creek at top; railroad along Klemm. Own title and scale; no index. Today in Gloucester City.
